newsitem.title: USA: Top U.S. Asia official visiting China.
newsitem.headline: Top U.S. Asia official visiting China.

text.p: The U.S. State Department's top Asia official, Winston Lord, is on a previously unannounced visit to China to discuss the full range of issues between Washington and Beijing, the department said on Tuesday.

Spokesman Nicholas Burns said Lord, Assistant Secretary of State for East Asian and Pacific Affairs, was preparing for a visit next month by Secretary of State Warren Christopher, but that "all issues are on the table".

Burns told a news briefing that Lord had gone to China after a visit last week to South Korea to discuss tensions over the beaching of a North Korean submarine on the South Korean coast last month. Lord would also visit Japan later this week, Burns said.

U.S. officials say relations with China have generally improved in recent months, but there have been frictions in the last two weeks over its treatment of dissidents and over fresh reports of Chinese nuclear sales to Pakistan.

"I think all issues are on the table in (Lord's) discussions with the Chinese. It wouldn't surprise me at all if that issue of the alleged sale of items between China and Pakistan came up," Burns said. He added that human rights issues were also likely to be raised.
Christopher is due to visit China Nov. 21-22.
